names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 11 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Αειθαλάς και Ακεψεής», with the rank word left off.

Read from the calendar’s own name page, «Акепсий Арбесский (Персидский), мч.», with the rank stripped and both epithets kept as the page prints them, the parenthesis included; the day line declines it as «Акепсия». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 11 декабря ст. ст. — «Мчч. Акепсия и Аифала (354).»

attestations.note: The first of the two the day’s second line names, on the same menologion day the Greek calendar keeps the pair on. The reading at /Life/life3103.htm is the first account the folder has had of either man, and it gives this one an office the Greek entry did not: a pagan priest at Arbela, healed of a sickness by a Christian bishop’s prayers and converted by it. `dates` ARE WRITTEN FOR THE FIRST TIME from the line’s «(354)» alone, the reading giving no year; the same year goes on his companion’s folder. The day page prints four hymns and none is under either name.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 11ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Αειθαλάς και Ακεψεής»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 11 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The entry names both its members and gives each his rank, so it is one folder per named member and each relates the other. His name, Ἀκεψεής, is not the Ἀκεψιμάς of the same day's separate entry for Peter the ascetic, nor the Akepsimas of 29 January the corpus already keeps, nor the one of 7 December drafted in this run; the four are kept apart because the calendar keeps them apart. No year, so no `dates` object. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (2 October 2026).

death.note: The year the Russian day line closes with, «Мчч. Акепсия и Аифала (354)»; the folder had no date at all before, the Greek calendar giving none, and the reading behind the line gives none either.
